segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Honor your father and mother,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: which is the first commandment with a promise,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “so that it may go well with you and you may live long on the earth.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Slaves, obey your earthly masters with fear and trembling, in sincerity of heart, as you would Christ,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: not serving only when watched, as people-pleasers, but as slaves of Christ doing the will of God, wholeheartedly

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: serving with goodwill, as for the Lord and not for people,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: knowing that whatever good each person does, this he will receive back from the Lord, whether slave or free.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And masters, do the same to them, giving up threats, knowing that both their Master and yours is in the heavens, and there is no favoritism with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Put on the full armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: because our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore take up the full armor of God, so that you may be able to withstand on the evil day and, having done everything, to stand.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Stand, then, with truth belted around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness on,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and with your feet shod in the readiness of the good news of peace,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: in every situation taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to put out all the flaming arrows of the evil one.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: through every prayer and petition, praying on every occasion in the Spirit, and to that end keeping watch with all perseverance and petition for all the holy ones,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and for me, that a word may be given to me when I open my mouth, to make known boldly the secret of the good news,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for which I am an ambassador in chains, so that in declaring it I may speak boldly, as I must.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So that you also may know how things are with me and what I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will make everything known to you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I am sending him to you for this very purpose, that you may know how we are and that he may encourage your hearts.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peace to the brothers and sisters, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with undying love.

notes.note: This translation normally renders this adjective as “righteous” or “just”, but here it describes a course of action, not a person, and plain English says “this is right”, as most versions do. Greek has a single word-family where English has two (right/righteous/righteousness and just/justice), so the same root lies behind “the breastplate of righteousness” in verse 14.

The quotation is the commandment of Exodus 20:12 and Deuteronomy 5:16 in its Greek form. There the promise concerns long life in “the land that the Lord your God is giving you”, and the Greek word can mean either “land” or “earth”. The letter leaves out the clause about the land God is giving, which makes the promise read as a general one.

notes.traditional: doing the will of God from the heart
notes.note: The Greek phrase, literally “from the soul”, sits between two clauses and can attach to either. Most English versions join it to what precedes (“doing the will of God from the heart”). The punctuation of the Greek edition translated here joins it to what follows (“wholeheartedly serving with goodwill”), and the translation follows that.

notes.traditional: your Master / their Lord and yours
notes.note: Greek uses one word, kyrios, for both a slave’s “master” and “the Lord”. Throughout verses 5–9 the passage plays on this: slaves serve earthly masters as serving the Lord, and masters are reminded that they have a Master of their own. English has to choose between “master” and “Lord” each time, which hides the repetition.

The Greek is plural, a turn of phrase carried over from Hebrew and from the Greek Old Testament. Most English translations flatten it to “heaven”. This translation keeps the plural where the Greek has it.

The verb can mean “accomplish, carry through” or “overcome, subdue”. Most translations take it as having made every preparation or done all that the fight requires. On the other reading it means “having defeated all opponents”. Either fits the military picture.

The Greek leaves open how “readiness” relates to “the good news of peace”. It may be the readiness or firm footing that the good news gives, or a readiness to go and announce it. The rendering keeps the Greek’s open phrasing; commentators are divided.

“Gospel” has become a religious term and a book title. The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news, used also of imperial proclamations. Many modern translations already alternate between “gospel” and “good news”.

“Saints” now suggests canonised individuals or people of unusual virtue. The Greek word is used of all members of the community as people set apart for God, echoing the Greek Old Testament’s language for Israel. Many translations keep “saints”; others use “God’s people”.

The traditional “mystery” suggests to a modern reader something puzzling or beyond understanding. In the usage of the period, including the Greek book of Daniel, the word means a secret, here one that God kept hidden and has now disclosed, which is why it can be “made known”. Most English versions keep “mystery”, and scholars generally explain it in this sense.

The verb is the ordinary term for serving as an official envoy. Envoys were by long custom treated as inviolable, so an ambassador in chains is a deliberate paradox. The Greek word for “chain” is singular.

The Greek plural was the normal way to address or refer to a mixed group of men and women as members of one family, and here it means the whole community. Older versions have “brethren” or “brothers”; several modern translations render it as here. In verse 21 the singular refers to one man and is translated “brother”.

The letter’s last words are literally “in imperishability”, and what they modify is disputed. They may describe the love of those who love Christ, as translated here and in most versions. They may instead go with “grace” (“grace and immortality be with all…”), or describe Christ as the one who lives in immortality.

candidates.reason: Recurs in the Gospels, Paul and Revelation; translators divide between “mystery” and “secret”, and a reader would be misled if the two alternated across chapters.

candidates.rendering: brothers and sisters (plural, of the community)
candidates.reason: The generic plural occurs in nearly every letter and in Acts, and “brothers” versus “brothers and sisters” needs a single policy.
Translations vary between “slave”, “servant” and “bondservant”; it must stay distinct from διάκονος and consistent in phrases such as “slaves of Christ”.
Occurs across John, Acts, Paul, Hebrews and 1 John with renderings ranging over “boldness”, “confidence”, “openly” and “plainly”; the senses need to be mapped once.
Paired repeatedly with ἀρχή for cosmic powers and also used for “authority”, “right” and “power”; consistent English for each sense is needed across the letters.

patch.reason: euangelion promoted to active after full-run drift (good news 37 / gospel 35)
